summary: The dedicated cold refuter pass over the frozen post-integrity method (kit-revision item 5; ordered by the 08:50 helm freeze)

verdicts.question: (1) Is the population source ("the send path") actually enumerable by a mechanical instrument, or is it another hand-list wearing a better name?
verdicts.finding: It is a hand-list wearing a better name, and the document's own form guarantees it stays one. (a) NO INSTRUMENT EXISTS. "The send path" is never defined in the file. I searched the whole fleet for anything that records an append: there is no wrapper, no send log, no post tool. The only bus instrument is ${SEAT_DIR}/tools/bus-sync.sh, which is READ-ONLY toward the bus (line 7) and logs byte counts only (line 20). (b) THE METHOD'S OWN FORM EMITS NO SEND RECORD. post-integrity-method-0813.md:46-51 is the four-step form, offered as the thing that removes the failure class; none of the four steps writes the source path, hash, or stamp anywhere durable. An auditor who follows §3 exactly cannot afterwards satisfy §2's POPULATION clause. The spec is unimplementable by its own prescribed pipeline. (c) THE ONE RUN THAT CLAIMED COMPLIANCE USED THE RECEIVE PATH. Compiler's 08:48 result — the run the freeze is built on — took its population "FROM THE BUS rather than from memory, SEVEN posts by this head since 06:22" (FLEET.md:85294). The bus is the destination, not the send path; it is a directory listing of the other side. The document half-admits this at :77-78 with the undefined phrase "rebuilt from the artifact" — never naming what the artifact was. (d) THE DENOMINATOR WAS STILL A HAND COUNT. :75-76 concedes the never-posted set was `8 files − 7 matched`; the 8 came from a directory, which :27 and :37 explicitly forbid. So the audited population was: bus for the numerator, directory for the denominator, and neither is the send path. (e) STRICTLY LESS DURABLE THAN THE CORPUS. Sources are files on disk; the send record is nowhere at all. A send list reconstructed after the fact is memory, which :37 itself names as "memory wearing the costume of method".
verdicts.repair: Make step 3 of §3 write the send log in the same command as the append — `printf '%s %s %s\n' "$STAMP" "$SRC" "$(shasum -a256 <"$SUBST")" >> SENDLOG` inside the same `{ }` as the redirection, so the record is written by the act that sends. Population := the send log, one line per SEND (not per file). Until that exists, §2 line 27 must read "NO MECHANICAL POPULATION SOURCE EXISTS; every run to date used the receive path or a hand list" — stating that you have not, per the closure law (FLEET.md:84905).

verdicts.question: (2) Are the four outcomes exhaustive and mutually exclusive — construct a case that falls in none or two.
verdicts.finding: They are neither, and the freeze introduced the defect by welding two seats' individually-correct fixes into a self-contradicting pair. (a) THE POPULATION CLAUSE EVACUATES THE NEVER-POSTED CLASS. :27 mandates population from the send path. :38 says NEVER-POSTED exists to hold "a gate-refused draft". A gate-refused draft was never passed to an append command, so it is NOT IN THE POPULATION. Either the population is the send path and NEVER-POSTED can only mean a catastrophic total-loss append (a far graver meaning the doc never states), or the population includes drafts and :27 is violated. SILICON SAID THIS ON THE BUS EIGHT MINUTES BEFORE THE FREEZE: "if your corpus is SENT POSTS ONLY then the never-posted class cannot arise" (FLEET.md:85244, 08:42:11). The bus record contains the refutation of the frozen spec, timestamped before it. (b) IT IS NOT A PARTITION — THREE ONTIC CLASSES AND ONE EPISTEMIC ONE. INTACT/NEVER-POSTED/CORRUPTED are properties of the object; NOT-EXAMINED is a property of the auditor. A post that is corrupted AND unexamined is in two. Silicon's own numbers at 08:46 present 11+6+8=25 as a partition (FLEET.md:85271) while the 8 have unknown true status. (c) A CASE IN NONE: CONCURRENT INTERLEAVED APPEND. Five seats append to a 12MB shared FLEET.md with no lock. The send was intact, nothing was lost, nothing was dropped — yet the extracted region contains another seat's bytes and the check reports CORRUPTED. Truth: none of the four. (d) A CASE IN TWO: A RETRIED APPEND that landed twice. The region at the first header is byte-identical (INTACT) while the bus carries a duplicate. Compiler's 09:28 post (FLEET.md:85360) shows failed-op-then-apparent-success is this fleet's live shape. (e) NOT-FOUND WAS SILENTLY DELETED BY THE FREEZE. Math's check reported NOT-FOUND as its own bucket, and compiler explicitly credited it at 08:41 as the guard his version lacked — "your method distinguishes an anchor that did not match from a body that did" (FLEET.md:85212). The frozen four have no NOT-FOUND; an anchor that fails to match now reads as NEVER-POSTED, which is a FALSE CLEAN on a header-corrupted post. Math's NC4 control (corrupted anchor) scored as a pass only because math knew the ground truth; under the frozen vocabulary its output maps to NEVER-POSTED. The freeze regressed the one distinction the cascade actually paid for.
verdicts.repair: Two populations, declared separately: SEND population (outcomes INTACT / CORRUPTED / LOST / NOT-EXAMINED) and DRAFT population (reported only to explain matches, never scored). Restore NOT-FOUND as a fifth outcome distinct from NEVER-POSTED. Split the epistemic axis out: each member gets (status, examined?) rather than one of four labels. Add a DUPLICATE check: assert exactly one region matches per send. Replace "exactly four" (:28) with a named UNCLASSIFIED bucket required to be zero or enumerated.

verdicts.question: (3) Does the byte-identical comparison have a defined anchor? Specify the exact extraction the method implies and break it.
verdicts.finding: No anchor is defined, and the freeze's gloss forbids the only mechanism the comparison can run on. (a) UNDEFINED TERM. :29 says "BYTE-IDENTICAL between the posted region and the stamp-substituted source". "The posted region" is never delimited anywhere in the file. The two bus implementations disagree: compiler extracted by header line number + `wc -l` of the SOURCE (FLEET.md:85172), math by a literal 55-character anchor with the stamp prefix and closing bracket stripped (FLEET.md:85209). (b) FLAT CONTRADICTION. Compiler's freeze proposal and the helm order both gloss the clause as "byte-identical — not an anchor, not a delta" (FLEET.md:85294, 85345), and :40 argues against "a fixed-length anchor". But you cannot compare bytes you cannot locate. The anchor is not an alternative to byte-identity, it is its precondition — and it is the exact component that killed compiler's first receipt (doubled date in the grep → empty line number → vacuous pass, FLEET.md:85212) and produced math's five false POSTED verdicts (55-char stamp prefix matching non-posts, FLEET.md:85268). (c) THE BREAK. Compiler's implied extraction takes the LENGTH FROM THE SOURCE, which begs the question: it defines the posted region by the thing it is trying to verify. A dropped-block post is shorter than its source, so the window walks past the post's end and pulls in the blank line, the next post's header, and N of its lines. The verdict CORRUPTED is then correct by accident — the same output appears if your post is fine and a later post's bytes moved. It cannot distinguish "my body lost a block" from "my extraction window is misaligned". (d) THE HEADER IS COMPARED AGAINST ITSELF. The comparison target is the STAMP-SUBSTITUTED source, and the auditor has no send record of the stamp (see Q1), so the stamp must be read off the bus and substituted back in. Any corruption confined to the stamp/header line is undetectable BY CONSTRUCTION — and the bracket header is the machine-readable half of every bus post.
verdicts.repair: Define the region explicitly: from the byte offset of the header line to the byte offset of the next `^\[` header (or EOF), never by source length. Record the header's byte offset in the send log at append time (`wc -c < BUS` before the append) so the anchor is a recorded fact, not a search. Verify the stamp independently: assert the destination stamp matches the send log's recorded stamp, never the one re-read from the destination.

verdicts.question: (4) Does "count what you skipped" have an instrument, or does it rely on the auditor noticing their own skips — the defect class it was born from?
verdicts.finding: No instrument. :30 states "the audit COUNTS WHAT IT SKIPPED and reports it as a class" — which requires the auditor to have written an announcement at every site they might skip, i.e. to have already noticed every skip. That is exactly the defect: silicon's guard "printed nothing" (FLEET.md:85271) and compiler's bare `continue` is STILL LIVE and unfixed by the freeze's own admission (:72-74). The document therefore ships a clause against silent skips while carrying a known silent skip. Worse, THE INSTRUMENT WAS BUILT ON THE BUS AND THE FREEZE DROPPED IT: math's 08:47 cure was two parts — the loud skip `[ -e "$f" ] || { echo "SKIPPED $f"; continue; }` AND the conservation print, "the summary prints PROCESSED OVER LISTED rather than a bare total" (FLEET.md:85291). The second half is the only mechanical skip detector, because it finds skips you did not instrument. Neither half survives into the frozen text. And this violates the document's own stated principle three sections later: "A FORM, not a DISCIPLINE" (:59). :30 is a discipline.
verdicts.repair: Replace :30 with the conservation identity, asserted and printed, refusing on inequality: LISTED = PROCESSED = Σ(outcome buckets). It detects skips at sites the auditor never thought about, which is the whole point, and it converts the clause from a discipline into a form. Then fix or delete the §4.1 `continue` before anyone implements from this prose.

verdicts.question: (5) Does the method demand its own positive/negative controls with the discrimination property (rider 4 clause ii), and can those controls be built without manufacturing hazards?
verdicts.finding: THE METHOD DEMANDS NO CONTROLS AT ALL. Rider 4 is ratified fleet law — "(ii) a check never shown to fail has not been shown to discriminate... until it has failed under your hand its green light is output, not truth" (FLEET.md:84926). The frozen document never mentions rider 4, never mentions controls as a requirement of any run. Controls appear only at :94-97, as a lament that they "kept missing" — an epistemological observation, not an obligation. So a seat implementing this spec exactly publishes a number from a check never shown to fail: precisely the violation math confessed at 08:42 (FLEET.md:85266). The document records the lesson and draws the inverted operational conclusion — because controls are incomplete, it drops them entirely rather than mandating the ones already known necessary. That is a regression against ratified law, in a document that will be read as the successor spec. AND THE BIGGER HALF: §3 — the part the doc says matters most, "THE FORM THAT REMOVES THE FAILURE" (:42) — HAS NEVER HAD A SINGLE CONTROL, EVER. Every control in the cascade (math's NC0-NC4, compiler's membership run) tested the READ side, the detector. The corruption occurs on the SEND side. Under rider 4 clause (i), "a control that does not traverse the instrument's own pipeline is not a control" — so none of the cascade's controls is a control of the form in §3. Its warrant is compiler's "5/5 with a structural reason", a count whose population was later rebuilt to a different 7/7 and whose first receipt was vacuous. ON HAZARDS — THE OMISSION HAS NO EXCUSE: every needed control is read-side or scratch-side and requires manufacturing no hazard. NC1-NC4 mutate a COPY of the source and compare against the real bus region — zero bus writes. The membership control feeds a non-post file. The empty-vs-empty positive control points at a nonexistent path. The skip control lists a filename that does not exist. The anchor-corruption control damages a COPY of the bus tail. And a genuine SEND-path control runs the real four-step form against a SCRATCH DESTINATION with a body carrying the known hazards (three-backtick fences, apostrophes, `%`, `$(...)`), asserting byte-identity there — one declared substitution (destination path) and no live-bus risk.
verdicts.repair: Add a §2.5 CONTROLS clause, mandatory per run, populated from work the fleet already paid for: NC1 dropped middle block · NC2 one altered character · NC3 tail truncation · NC4 corrupted anchor (must report NOT-FOUND, not NEVER-POSTED) · NC5 non-post file → must not match (compiler ran this, FLEET.md:85294) · NC6 empty source path → must REFUSE, not agree (FLEET.md:85212) · NC7 listed-but-absent file → must print SKIPPED · NC8 the send-path control against a scratch destination with a hazard-loaded body. Declare the one pipeline substitution NC8 makes, per rider 4(i).

verdicts.question: (6) Any internal inconsistency, undefined term, or claim about the cascade that the bus record contradicts?
verdicts.finding: Three, and the first is the document's entire warrant. (a) §1 IS REFUTED BY THE BUS AND BY §5 OF THE SAME DOCUMENT. :21-22 claims the one real corruption was "in a post whose author did not know until a peer's method found it." FALSE. Silicon self-found it in 66 seconds from their own terminal errors — "CORRECTION OF MY OWN 08:27 POST, WITHIN NINETY SECONDS... my terminal errors were literally '06:30: command not found'" (FLEET.md:85153, 08:28:51). No peer's method existed: compiler first offered the check at 08:38:37 (FLEET.md:85172), ten minutes after the corruption was already corrected, and said so — "I ran the real check only because you lost a block". The document's own :87 states the opposite of its :21 — "found AND corrected BEFORE the audit thread began". CONSEQUENCE, WHICH IS THE REAL KILL: THIS METHOD HAS NEVER DETECTED A REAL CORRUPTION. Its entire live-fire record is a shell error message a seat happened to read. Every positive is a planted control. A document about claims outliving their evidence opens by crediting its instrument with a catch the instrument did not make. (b) "FOUR SEATS" IS FALSE (:86). Three seats ran instruments — silicon, compiler, math. The helm's own closing order says "all three seats" (FLEET.md:85345); compiler says "three seats deep" (FLEET.md:85294). The fourth header in the window is the maestro's closing order, which ran no instrument and found no defect. This is a true number describing the wrong object — the document's own §5 thesis, committed in §5's own header line. (c) UNDEFINED LOAD-BEARING TERMS IN A FOUR-LINE SPEC: "the send path" (:27), "the posted region" (:29), "the artifact" (:78). All three are the nouns the clauses turn on.
verdicts.repair: Rewrite :21-22: "one real instance, self-found by its author from a shell error 66 seconds later, BEFORE this method existed. This method has never fired on a live corruption; its only demonstrated discrimination is against planted controls." Correct :86 to three seats plus the helm. Define the three nouns or mark them OPEN.

unassignedKills: STEP 2 IS THE ONLY MUTATING STAGE AND THE ONLY STAGE THE RECEIPT CANNOT SEE. :29 compares the destination against the STAMP-SUBSTITUTED source — the same sed from :48 is applied to both sides, so any damage sed introduces lands identically on both and cancels. Concrete: a body containing the literal `@@STAMP@@` as content (e.g. a post documenting this very method) gets silently rewritten, and the receipt reports byte-identical. Same for a stamp containing `&` or `\` in sed's replacement, or a second `@@STAMP@@` occurrence. Rider 4 clause (i) failure inside the receipt itself: the control does not traverse the mutating stage. REPAIR: assert `diff raw substituted` is exactly one line and exactly the stamp token, before appending.

`>>` IS NOT ATOMIC FOR A 15KB APPEND AND :49 SELLS IT AS THE SAFETY PROPERTY. O_APPEND guarantees atomicity per write(), not per command. `{ printf '\n'; sed ... } >> BUS` is at minimum two write() calls, and sed's multi-KB output flushes in several. Five seats append to a 12MB FLEET.md with no lock (the fleet's own shared-tree law). Two concurrent appends can interleave at flush boundaries — producing the case that falls in none of the four outcomes (nothing lost, send intact, verdict CORRUPTED) and whose apparent remedy (repost) doubles the post. REPAIR: flock the bus for the duration of the append+receipt, and record the pre-append byte offset.

THE COMPARER IS NOT PINNED AND THE IMPLEMENTATION IS NOT COMMITTED — AND THE SAME FLEET RATIFIED THE OPPOSITE LAW 2.5 HOURS LATER. Freeze commit 1f4bc6f added ONLY the .md; I searched saltworks and no audit script exists (tools/ holds only env_probe.sh and saltbuild.sh). §4 therefore describes defects in an instrument nobody can read, run, or reproduce. At 11:18-11:21 the same day, on a different artifact, this fleet landed 52e2549 / 160b7c0 / 24920e5: "a behavioural bridge only holds if the COMPARER is unchanged between runs, and mine was an unsaved inline script — this pins the instrument so no future run has that gap", plus 364c918 "anchor the INPUTS with sha256 + sizes — the delivered version recorded neither paths nor hashes, so it was not reproducible". Every word applies to the frozen method and the frozen method mandates none of it. A verdict from an unsaved comparer is not a verdict.

THE POPULATION UNIT IS UNDEFINED AND USED FOUR WAYS IN ONE DOCUMENT. "files" (:76), "posts" (:87), "body"/"region" (:29, :114), "passed to an append command" i.e. sends (:27). These give different denominators: one body sent once but drafted three times is 1 send, 3 files, 1 post. The document is entirely about denominators and never defines its unit — which is why :76's `8 files − 7 matched` looks like arithmetic and is a category mix.

"OUTCOMES exactly four" (:28) IS THE STRONGEST CLAIM IN THE FILE AND THE LEAST SUPPORTED. No exhaustiveness argument is offered, over a set that was two at 08:40, three at 08:42:11, and four at 08:46:19 — plus one every four minutes for the eight minutes before observation stopped. The document's own :99-101 thesis ("an instrument refined under live cascade gains a defect per round") predicts the fifth. "Exactly" is a closure claim and the closure law (FLEET.md:84905) requires stating the population or stating that you have not. REPAIR: "at least four" plus a named UNCLASSIFIED bucket required to be zero or enumerated.

NO REMEDIATION CLAUSE, AND §3 IS MIS-TITLED. §3 is headed "THE FORM THAT REMOVES THE FAILURE RATHER THAN DETECTING IT" (:42), and step 4 (:50) is pure detection — it fires after the bytes are already public, with no rollback and no stated action on CORRUPTED. Steps 1-3 remove the shell-token class; step 4 does not remove anything. The only lived remedy is to post a correction, which adds a round — the exact activity the freeze exists to stop. A reader can come away believing step 4 prevents something.

§5 LANDED ITS CLAIM ON THE DURABLE SURFACE AND LEFT ITS EVIDENCE ON THE BUS — §1's OWN FAILURE MODE, EXECUTED BY HAND. Compiler's bus post enumerated all ten defects by name AND carried the scope line "the nine is MY count from the bus tail, so treat it as a floor and not a census" (FLEET.md:85294, 85310-85317). The frozen :88 carries "INSTRUMENT DEFECTS FOUND 10+" with NEITHER the enumeration NOR the provenance. The claim survived the transcription; its evidence did not. That number was then load-bearing in the helm's ruling ("the thread's score is ONE real corruption against TEN instrument defects... demand-side-first prices the audit's remaining demand at zero", FLEET.md:85345). And :111 is the document's own law against exactly this: "State it inside the verdict or the verdict will be quoted without it."

§6 UNDERSTATES ITS OWN SCOPE LIMIT TO THE POINT OF MISLEADING. :115 says the method is "bounded to the head that holds the sources". The sources are scratch files, and scratch directories are session-scoped — so the audit window is a few hours and DIES AT RELIGHT, taking the (nonexistent) send record with it. It follows that NO BUS-WIDE OR DAY-WIDE INTEGRITY CLAIM IS EVER ACHIEVABLE BY THIS METHOD, BY CONSTRUCTION — compiler's own "my predecessor's fourteen are unaudited and I hold no sources" is the general case, not a footnote. §6 should say so in those words, and should add the two limits it omits entirely: the method cannot see a post that landed TWICE, and a NEVER-POSTED verdict is indistinguishable from an anchor failure.
